capturedFrom: the original T-SQL object, deployed unchanged to a scratch SQL Server database with the fixed case's rows
review: Captured from the source engine, not derived independently. A reviewer checks each case's expected values against its label at step 5 (second review). Values are canonical: n: number, s: text, b: bit, d: date, t: timestamp (microseconds), x: bytes (hex), ∅: NULL.

cases.label: [A01] status 8 (second unmapped value above the last WHEN) is the ELSE text
[A02] status 127 (signed 1-byte maximum) is the ELSE text
[A03] status 128 (one above the signed 1-byte maximum) is the ELSE text, not an error
[A04] status 254 (one below the tinyint maximum) is the ELSE text
[A05] status 134 (6 + 128, same low bits as 'Cancelled') is the ELSE text
[A06] status 3 gives 'Backordered', the longest mapped text (11 characters), from a varchar literal into nvarchar(15)
